subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB340, LANDED. Rule text re-validated: cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'If the ADVANCING ON LOCK phrase is specified on the READ statement of a file open for file sharing and the record to be made available is locked by another file connector, the result of this READ statement is as if the locked record were read and then the same READ statement were executed.' -> OK 14.9.30.4 22). THE SKIP-SCAN IS NOW ONE MECHANISM FOR ALL THREE ORGANIZATIONS. GR22 is a FORMAT-1 rule, not a sequential-ORGANIZATION one: ADVANCING appears only in the Format-1 general format (14.9.30.2) and SR6 bars it under ACCESS MODE RANDOM, so it reaches sequential, relative and indexed alike. FileRegistry.ReadShared was rewritten as the one governed Format-1 read for every organization (it returns the I-O status; a record was made available iff it begins '0'), with the physical step behind ReadFormat1Step and the pre-read lock identity behind PeekFormat1RecordId. The GR22 skip is written ONCE, post-read, because the rule's own model is post-read ('as if the locked record were read and then the same READ statement were executed') and because 'A record operation conflict condition does not exist', so GR10 a) never applies to it. KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead routes KeyedReadKind.Next/Previous through that entry; the Format-2 random read goes through FileRegistry.ReadKeyedShared, which owns that format's retrieval (there is no next record to advance to, and no ADVANCING phrase in the Format-2 general format). Previously the loop lived only inside the sequential arm and BoundKeyedRead.AdvancingOnLock was read nowhere in KeyedIoEmitter, so a relative or indexed READ ADVANCING ON LOCK answered '51'. TESTS: the two 2002 goldens cover the repeated skip (two locked records skipped, the third made available), the SR9 spelling with neither NEXT nor an at-end phrase, the PREVIOUS direction, and BOTH tails - end of file for NEXT and beginning of file for PREVIOUS, each landing on GR24's '10' and the AT END imperative - with a plain READ NEXT '51' control in each program proving the locks were really in the way; expected values are derived per leg in the program headers from GR21/GR22/GR24/GR25 and matched on the first run. The two negative goldens pin the COBOL-2002 edition gate (COBOL0900) on BOTH the keyed and the sequential arm, which nothing exercised before - the version-matrix row for the record-lock family writes READ ... WITH LOCK. unit:BoundIoPhraseConsumptionDriftTests.EveryPhrasePropertyOfABoundIoNode_IsReadByItsEmitter now fails if any phrase property of a bound I-O node goes unread by its emitter, which is the shape this row was an instance of. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: unchanged - 2002 - 2014 - 2023 (Annex A.4.7 'File sharing and record locking', Claimed in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 5; Annex E records no change from 2014).
